body:
Global crypto market cap sits at $2.79T this Friday, with the 24-hour change registering a slight negative at -0.34% despite meaningful price gains across most majors — a discrepancy that points to composition shifts and rotation rather than net new money entering the space. Volume across all tracked assets came in at an enormous $80,550.7B over 24 hours, suggesting this is an active, liquid session rather than a thin drift higher. The Fear & Greed Index jumped from 53 (Neutral) yesterday to 63 (Greed) today, a meaningful single-session move in sentiment that traders should not dismiss — rapid sentiment shifts of that magnitude can precede either acceleration or sharp mean reversion, and positioning accordingly matters. BTC dominance holds at 59.3% with ETH dominance at 10.8%, and the spread between those two figures is worth flagging as altcoin outperformance begins to narrow the gap in a meaningful way.

Bitcoin traded at $82,455, up 2.03% over 24 hours and a modest +0.49% on the hour, but the 7-day return of just +0.08% tells the real story: BTC has been grinding sideways on the weekly timeframe while alts run. Volume of $32.24B is healthy and not indicative of a low-conviction pop, but the market structure here is cautious. According to CryptoQuant analysis cited by Cointelegraph, Bitcoin may need to reclaim a 20-month trend line before mounting a credible run at new record highs — that qualitative framing aligns with the flat 7-day performance and suggests the $82,455 level is more of a consolidation zone than a confirmed breakout. Watch the downside for any loss of the recent range low, and on the upside, a clean daily close materially above current levels with volume expansion would be the first signal that the trend-line reclaim thesis is playing out.

ETH at $2,471.81 is the standout large-cap performer today, up 4.80% in 24 hours on $14.75B in volume — strong participation relative to its market weight. Chainlink at $12.67 added 5.14% with $0.35B in volume, a quiet but consistent performer. The real action was in the second tier: UNI surged 8.42% to $7.44 on $0.62B in volume, the best 24-hour return among ZIMR-tracked majors, while AVAX gained 7.41% to $10.26 and DOT jumped 7.42% to $1.17 despite being one of the quieter names most sessions. SOL added 4.21% to $106.33 on $3.3B in volume, respectable on an absolute basis, though its 7-day print of -2.88% shows it has ground to make up. The laggards are clear: BNB was essentially flat in relative terms at +1.55% to $730.59, XRP added only 2.98% to $1.34 but carries a painful 7-day loss of -2.85%, and BNB's 7-day decline of -1.30% reinforces that the Binance ecosystem is underperforming this rotation. The headline citing Celestia jumping 16% on the session adds further color to the breadth of this altcoin move, though Celestia is not in the ZIMR tracked universe.

The macro context is layered and, frankly, unsettled in ways that could cut either direction. Federal Reserve Governor Warsh is reportedly silent on interest-rate plans, per headline, which is itself a signal — ambiguity from a hawkish Fed figure keeps rate-cut expectations in flux and limits the conviction with which risk assets can re-rate higher. Circle targeting 40 new markets as stablecoin demand grows globally is a structural positive for crypto liquidity and adoption, and the Cointelegraph CONNECT recap flagging liquidity as tokenization's next challenge speaks to the same theme. On the risk side, a Quantum Alliance has formed amid warnings that 6.4 million bitcoin face a future quantum threat — this is early-stage and speculative, but the fact it is generating coordinated industry response means institutional risk desks are beginning to model it. Tokenized Tesla surging on the back of Elon Musk's SpaceX-powered Roadster reveal is a niche but illustrative data point: real-world asset tokenization is capturing retail imagination even in single-name equity tokens. A reported $78M first-half loss at Capital B driven by Bitcoin impairment charges is a reminder that levered Bitcoin treasury strategies carry meaningful balance sheet risk in range-bound markets.

Going into next week, 3 catalysts stand out. First, watch any rate commentary from Warsh or other Fed officials — a hawkish surprise would almost certainly cap this altcoin rally and push BTC back toward the lower end of its weekly range. Second, the court ruling rejecting the CFTC and Gemini bid to undo their $5M settlement is a small regulatory signal, but the broader direction of U.S. crypto regulation remains the single largest macro variable for the space; any movement on pending stablecoin legislation or spot ETF product expansions would be an immediate price catalyst. Third, the Solana Shanghai event postponement due to registration surge, as reported by Cointelegraph, is a genuine demand signal for the SOL developer ecosystem — when the event rescheduled date is announced, expect it to act as a near-term catalyst for SOL. The picture changes bearishly if BTC fails to reclaim that 20-month trend line and rolls over from current levels, dragging a market that has just rotated into risk with it; it changes bullishly if volume expansion accompanies another daily close above $82,455 and altcoin breadth holds through the weekend.
